title: "Microwave-induced eustress in Datura innoxia: Integrated photosynthetic, oxidative, and cellular responses to a low-dose hormetic elicitor"
author: "Khan, M. M. A., Batool, T., Ali, A., Khan, S. A., Naeem, M., & Mukarram, M."
date: 2026-08-01

::: {.venue-line}
Biocatalysis and Agricultural Biotechnology, 76, 104207
:::

**DOI:** [10.1016/j.bcab.2026.104207](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.bcab.2026.104207)

**Abstract**

Both biotic and abiotic stresses induce the production of reactive oxygen species (ROS),
compromising plant physiology. However, the effects of microwave radiation on plant physiology
remain poorly understood. We hypothesised that low-dose microwave radiation exposure would
induce ROS accumulation in the alkaloid-producing plant Datura innoxia. D. innoxia plants were
exposed to microwave radiation (2.45 GHz) for 0, 1, 2, 4, and 8 s, and physiological responses
were profiled across six parameter axes 48 h post-exposure. The 8-s exposure raised leaf surface
temperature to ~52→ C and proved lethal, whereas sub-lethal exposures (↑4 s; ↑35.6→ C) elicited a
coordinated stimulatory response. A 4-second treatment increased chlorophyll (~36%) and
electron transport rate (~70%) without impairing PSII integrity. Energy partitioning shifted from
passive (Y(NO)) to regulated (Y(NPQ)) thermal dissipation as exposure dose increased, with the
highest non-photochemical quenching at 4 s. A transient H2O2 burst at 2 s, visualised by DAB
staining and accompanied by a ~16% phenolic increase, preceded the photoprotective activation
at 4 s. Malondialdehyde content rose monotonically with dose but remained within physiological
range. Light microscopy revealed widened stomatal apertures at 2 s and prominently visible
guard-cell chloroplasts at 4 s. Collectively, these findings indicate that brief microwave exposure
operates as a non-damaging physical elicitor within a narrow dose window (↑4 s), offering a
novel non-chemical avenue for modulating photosynthesis and oxidative status in medicinal
plants. The sharp threshold between 4 s (stimulatory) and 8 s (lethal) underscores the dosimetric
precision required to exploit microwave eustress in biotechnological applications.
